cards.name: 2Strip
cards.summary: Two-strip Technicolor-style look. On the warm test photo the cream wall and highlights turn rose-pink, yellows go pink while the green plant drains to a cyan-grey (every output pixel has equal green and blue, so the picture is built from red and cyan only), saturation roughly halves and the image brightens slightly: a faded pink-and-cyan vintage palette.
avoid: greens and yellows lose their colour (the plant went cyan-grey): avoid when foliage or a yellow brand colour must stay true
skin goes pink and flat; for a gentler vintage tone use a Fuji / Kodak 2395 film LUT
PGD's render used the coarse 8x8x8 table baked inside the SpeedGrade .look, so Photoshop's own result may differ slightly in smooth gradients
cards.applies_to: photo / pixel content: as a Color Lookup adjustment layer it grades everything visible below it (clip it to one layer to limit it); the destructive route Image > Adjustments > Color Lookup needs a pixel layer
cards.how_to_apply: Layer > New Adjustment Layer > Color Lookup, then in Properties pick '2Strip.look' from the 3DLUT File list (Photoshop lists the shipped tables by file name), or Load 3D LUT... and browse to <Photoshop 2026 install folder>/Presets/3DLUTs/2Strip.look. By script: a Color Lookup layer can be created, but PGD found (2026-10-04) that it ignores LUT data passed by script and renders only from the profile its own dialog builds, so the route to try is recording one load of this file with ScriptListener and replaying that descriptor (not tested by PGD).
cards.notes: PGD thumbnail: applied (outside Photoshop): the look's baked LUT (the <LUT> table inside the SpeedGrade .look, 8^3) trilinear-interpolated in Python on the 640x360 test photo (top = result, bottom = untouched warm test photo); not a Photoshop render.

verified.note: Rose-pink highlights (236/207/155 -> 244/209/209), saturation x0.53, L 102 -> 115; G = B in every output pixel, so the image is two-colour red / cyan and the plant goes cyan-grey (58/71/37 -> 71/78/78), not pink.
